name: SOAR AI, Inc. (formerly Volato Group, Inc.)

profile.description: SOAR AI (Sovereign AI Resources), renamed from Volato Group effective October 19, 2026, is pivoting from private aviation to AI infrastructure. Through its merger with Alignment Engine Inc. it is developing an AI infrastructure campus in Ohio (154 MW available, path to 480 MW) for high-density GPU compute, and it also offers the Parslee AI document platform and Vaunt, a private aviation membership marketplace. Chris Ensey is CEO; the company is based in North Canton, Ohio.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): The company has wound down jet ownership and operations (selling most aviation assets to flyExclusive) and merged with Alignment Engine to become an AI infrastructure owner, but this pivot followed a failing aviation business and has produced no AI infrastructure revenue yet; Q1 2026 revenue fell 96% [1][3][4]. AI Deployment (1/2): Parslee, an internally built LLM-structuring layer for complex documents, moved into early paying pilots in Q3 2025, but revenue is immaterial [5]. Market Share (0/2): No measurable share in AI compute or AI software. Pipeline (2/2): In September 2026 SOAR signed two four-year take-or-pay orders with a large AI customer worth $1.17B, including about $133M of prepayments, for AMD GPU clusters starting December 31, 2026 and June 30, 2027 [2]. R&D Intensity (0/1): No disclosed R&D spending of note at a 13-employee company [1].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (1/4): The new 'Sovereign AI Resources' identity and earlier 'scalable software and data solutions' language are generic and have changed with each strategic turn, including the earlier planned M2i Global critical-minerals merger [3][5]. Community Impact (0/2): No charitable or community programs found. Employee Retention (0/2): Headcount has shrunk to 13 and the CEO changed from Matt Liotta to Chris Ensey during the pivot [1][3]. Insider Buying (0/2): No open-market insider purchases were identified; the company is funding itself through equity facilities, including an up-to-$1B purchase agreement [2].

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Growth stock on three available metrics (total weight 3). D/E of 3.1% scores 1.0 (x1) with only $107K of debt; revenue growth of -96.1% YoY scores 0.0 (x1); and profit margin of -11.8% scores 0.0 (x1) [1]. ROE (negative equity position flagged by NYSE American), Forward P/E, Forward PEG, and 5yr revenue CAGR (public only since a 2023 SPAC) are unavailable and excluded. Weighted sum 1.0/3 = 3.3, giving a score of 3. Liquidity floor cleared: 50.9M avg shares x $0.22 = $11.4M daily dollar volume, though 10-day volume of 4.5M shares implies only about $1.0M, right at the floor [1].

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): The core plan is physical AI compute capacity (power, cooling, and AMD GPU clusters at the Ohio campus), which AI demand supports rather than displaces, and $1.17B of take-or-pay orders show real customer demand [2]. Parslee, however, is a thin software layer that improving foundation models could commoditize, and the GPU-cloud model faces pricing and obsolescence risk [5]. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI revenue has been recognized yet; GPU orders begin December 31, 2026 and Parslee pilots are immaterial [2][5].

infinite_game.summary: Through Sinek's lens this is a company playing to survive the next quarter. In three years it has moved from fractional jet ownership to AI document software, then a planned critical-minerals merger, then AI data centers, while changing its name and CEO, carrying a going-concern opinion and an NYSE American equity deficiency notice [3][6][7]. There is no stable cause for people to rally around.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (0/3): Each identity (Volato aviation, Parslee AI, M2i minerals, SOAR AI) has been framed around the opportunity of the moment, not an enduring vision of a better future [3][5].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (0/2): Strategic moves were forced by losses, aircraft-sale wind-downs, and listing-standard deficiencies rather than chosen sacrifices for a long-term cause [6][7].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): Headcount fell to 13, the CEO role turned over during the pivot, and aviation staff transferred out with the fleet sale to flyExclusive, which leaves little organizational continuity [1][3].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): The company has abandoned its original business entirely, a dramatic shift, but Sinek's top score requires a pivot driven by the Just Cause; this one was driven by the failure of the aviation model [4][7].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No commentary was found that acknowledges or learns from AI cloud competitors; messaging centers on contract wins and inbound LOIs [2][4].

investment_thesis: The bull case is pure optionality. SOAR has $1.17B of four-year take-or-pay GPU orders from a large AI customer, with about $133M of contractual prepayments, starting December 31, 2026 and June 30, 2027, at an Ohio campus with 154 MW available and a path to 480 MW [2]. Against a market cap of about $12M, even partial execution would transform the company, and the Alignment Engine combination values that platform at about $500M [2]. Debt is negligible ($107K) and the up-to-$1B equity purchase facility gives a funding route [1][2].
thesis_continued: The bear case is existential. Revenue collapsed 96% as aviation was shed, the 2025 audit carried a going-concern paragraph, and NYSE American cited stockholders' equity deficiencies with a December 17, 2026 compliance deadline [6][7]. Building GPU capacity for a $1.17B contract needs far more capital than SOAR has ($9.1M cash), so heavy dilution through the equity facility (capped at $6M per day and 19.99% of shares without shareholder approval) is likely [1][2]. With 13 employees, a new CEO, and no record of operating data centers, execution risk is extreme.
key_catalysts: Financing and delivering the first AMD GPU cluster for the $1.17B take-or-pay contract by its December 31, 2026 start date [2]
Regaining NYSE American stockholders' equity compliance by the December 17, 2026 deadline after the Alignment Engine merger [7]
Monetizing Vaunt through flyExclusive's extended purchase option to raise non-dilutive cash [3]
key_risks: Going-concern doubt and possible delisting if equity deficiencies are not cured by December 17, 2026 [6][7]
Severe dilution from the up-to-$1B equity purchase facility needed to fund GPU and campus build-out on a ~$12M market cap [2]
Execution and counterparty risk on a single large AI customer contract with no operating data center track record [2]
